subject.title: feat(mxc): add Windows MXC sandbox backend

question: After the registration-mode guard is fixed, should OpenClaw accept the preview MXC SDK/native dependency boundary for an official external sandbox plugin?
rationale: This choice includes native executor binaries, a `node-pty` install script allowance, and argv-visible base64 sandbox config; automation can fix the registration bug but cannot decide the security/trust policy.

options.title: Fix registration, then approve exact head
options.body: Add the full-mode guard and regression test, then have maintainer/secops approve the final dependency graph and documented argv boundary before merge.

options.title: Pause for safer SDK transport
options.body: Hold this PR until the upstream MXC SDK exposes a non-argv config transport or a narrower package boundary.

options.title: Decline first-party packaging
options.body: Rework or close this as community/plugin-only experimentation if maintainers do not want OpenClaw to ship an official sandbox backend with this native dependency boundary.

recommendation.title: Fix registration, then approve exact head
recommendation.body: Add the full-mode guard and regression test, then have maintainer/secops approve the final dependency graph and documented argv boundary before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: Best available routing owner from adjacent OpenShell sandbox and plugin SDK history, with this PR already assigned to them live.
